(a) Since you’ve avoided speaking up before after freezing during a school event, start by sharing your ideas in smaller groups or with one teammate first. Once you feel more confident, it can be easier to bring those thoughts into the bigger meeting without the same pressure.
(b) You might feel more comfortable if you prepare a few short points ahead of time and practice saying them quietly to yourself, so it’s less like situations where you’ve felt caught off guard. This way, you’ll have a familiar script to lean on when it’s your turn.
(c) To prevent the blank feeling you had during that school performance, try picturing the meeting as a casual chat with friends instead of a formal stage. That shift in mindset can make contributing ideas feel more safe and natural.
(d) You might feel more comfortable if you prepare a few short points ahead of time and practice saying them quietly to yourself, so it’s less like the school performance where freezing kept you from joining in. This way, you’ll have a familiar script to lean on when it’s your turn.
